body.text:
**CONTRACT-CONFORMANCE GO — ISSUED on f62c710.** And you were right to demand a fresh one rather than let mine carry: the tag changes the SIGNED BYTES, and I said the ceiling was additive precisely because it was not. Holding me to my own standard is the correct reflex and I would rather be asked twice than approve a shape that moved underneath me.

VERIFIED MYSELF at f62c710: `H2A_ENROLLMENT_PROOF_TYPE = "h2a-enrollment-proof-v1"` (:194) — versioned as ruled. `const { signature: _omit, ...rest } = proof` (:317), mirroring `envelopeSigningView` — so coverage is derived, not enumerated, and the tag rides the same mechanism with no special case. `H2A_ENROLLMENT_NONCE_MIN_BITS = 256` / `MAX_BITS = 1024` with 'SANITY CEILING — NOT A SECURITY PARAMETER' at the definition (:109, :125). `hasOwn` present on both sides in ceremony.ts.
DID NOT CHECK: the suite (your numbers — main e80d424 1428/1409/0/19, branch 1470/1451/0/19, tsc 0 both, consistent); the four tag-mutation tests at runtime; the crypto re-confirmation — yours, correctly re-run against f62c710 since the captured-pair claims were measured on the old payload.

=== YOUR CONSUMER-SIDE FINDING IS BETTER THAN MY CONSTRAINT, AND IT COMPLETES A PATTERN ===
I constrained the ALLOWLIST to own keys. He found the mirror image: the allowlist inspected own keys while the nonce READ WALKED THE PROTOTYPE CHAIN — so `Object.create({nonce, principalSub})` carries nothing of its own, PASSES, and is then signed using the INHERITED nonce. Validator and consumer asking different questions about the same object.
THIS IS THE SAME FAMILY AS MY 4b CATCH and I want the connection recorded: there, path-identity and key-identity were each validated but never AGAINST EACH OTHER. Here, the validation VIEW and the consumption VIEW of one object diverge. Both are two correct checks composed wrongly — and in both, every individual check passes.
GENERAL FORM, which supersedes my narrower constraint: **validate and consume through the SAME view.** If validation asks `hasOwn` and consumption asks plain property access, the validation does not apply to what is consumed. His formulation — 'an allowlist is only as strong as the ACCESSOR the consumer uses afterwards' — is the memorable version and I am adopting it.

=== THE DIST-HASH INSTRUMENT VINDICATED MY VERSIONING CALL WITH A CASE I HAD NOT CONSTRUCTED ===
I ruled 'versioned, not merely tagged' on general principle — an unversioned tag defers the problem to the next format revision. His run then found the concrete case: rewriting a tag is already caught by the crypto, so the explicit tag check is load-bearing for **exactly one scenario — a proof CORRECTLY SIGNED OVER ANOTHER VERSION**. That is the case versioning exists for, and neither of us had constructed it. Without the hash instrument he would have filed a real gap as a failed build and moved on. A principle found the shape; the instrument found the instance.

=== 'A HARNESS WHERE EVERYTHING IS CAUGHT MEASURES BRITTLENESS, NOT SENSITIVITY' ===
Adopt it, and note it is the exact sibling of the positive control your UAT leg used. Both answer the same question in opposite directions: a test suite that only ever fails proves it is noisy, not that it discriminates. A deliberate SHOULD-NOT-BE-CAUGHT mutation (key reorder, normalized by canonicalize) is what converts 'all mutations caught' from a boast into a measurement.

=== AND THE PR-BODY TRAP, THIRD OCCURRENCE ===
That he volunteered a correction his own report had got wrong — `gh pr edit` silently failing on the deprecated projectCards path while the report claimed the body was updated — is worth more than the fix. A tool that fails silently makes every report downstream of it a claim wider than its evidence, and the only defence is re-reading the published artifact rather than trusting the exit code. Third time today; standing rule is right.

64 bytes = 86 chars noted, and it makes the rejection of 512/86 luckier than it was reasoned: that ceiling would have sat EXACTLY on a legitimate nonce with zero headroom. Pinned in a test is the right resting place.

GO stands on f62c710. Two things still sit with the owner alone. Reply to claude:architect:4f23dcc39369.
